soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 / def:balanced-pool-design
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed polynomial-time deterministic algorithm requires exact comparisons of conditional potentials containing irrational exponentials, but gives neither an input encoding nor an approximation/slack guarantee showing that finite-precision branch choices preserve recovery and certificate claims.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 6–7, Theorems 2–3; p. 14, proof of Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 2 uses repeated singleton actions under ||Z_t||_1 ≤ B and has an n-squared graph-discovery term; Theorem 3 sets B=1 on disjoint pairs and gives an order-n discovery lower bound, explicitly noting the gap and possible sparsity tightening.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 6, Algorithm 2 and lines immediately following; pp. 6–7, Theorem 5.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Algorithm 2 fits each unknown-network row with Lasso over Fourier characteristics, and Theorem 5.1 provides its high-probability regret guarantee; it does not state a uniform exact-support recovery certificate.
The paper proves sparse-linear-bandit information-regret bounds under a well-conditioned exploration distribution, rather than a fixed-cardinality network-recovery problem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Target Estimand and Class of Estimators sections
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies heterogeneous additive network effects and total-treatment-effect estimation without knowing the network, which supports the stated use of it as an additive-interference comparator rather than a graph-recovery result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Give BP a bit-complexity specification: rationally approximate every conditional potential, state a numerical separation/slack invariant, and prove that the selected finite-precision branch retains the needed collision and sparse-eigenvalue guarantees.
Make the degree-s extension a named minimax object R*_(n,B,T,s), with an explicit candidate frontier or reward-information optimization and a concrete switching family on which it can be evaluated.

Add a scoped comparison to Gleich, Laber, and Volfovsky's AISTATS 2026 scalable-policy result and to Viviano–Rudder's cluster-based unknown-interference policy-design work, distinguishing fixed-graph certified recovery from their different regimes.

recommended_next_step: Revise the balanced-pool construction with a finite-precision computational guarantee, then advance the repaired field-tier matching-frontier kernel to Stage 0.
